briefing.opening: Good morning. As the specialized spokesperson for climate change, I will begin today's climate briefing on August 14, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Weather Events Striking the World and Their Severe Impacts
sections.content: Recently, extreme weather phenomena have intensified globally, causing severe damage. In Europe, a record-breaking heatwave re-emerged, with temperatures in central France soaring to 42.5℃, and Germany reported approximately 12,500 heat-related deaths, as the 'triple threat' of drought, heatwaves, and wildfires continues to impact the European economy [16, 22, 23, 101]. Domestically, the number of heatwave days in Gyeongsangbuk-do has doubled in 10 years, threatening the disappearance of natural reservoirs in mountainous areas due to the 'snow-eater' phenomenon, and the Jeonnam region, experiencing prolonged drought, required military water tankers to supply water for rice paddies [1, 6, 21]. Such climate changes are cited as the cause of a train derailment in southern England and have led to floods in India's Assam state, killing over 100 people and displacing thousands, demonstrating cascading impacts on daily life [7, 88, 113]. Furthermore, the butterfly effect of climate change is manifesting globally, with the Caspian Sea shrinking to historic low levels and northern agricultural lands transforming into concentrated nitrogen pollution zones [93, 100, 102].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Policies and Adaptation Efforts to Address the Climate Crisis
sections.content: The Republic of Korea is strengthening its policy and institutional framework to respond to the climate crisis. The National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate passed the Carbon Neutrality Act and the Climate Crisis Adaptation Act, taking the first step towards legislating climate crisis response [10, 20, 29, 50]. At the local government level, Gyeongsangbuk-do is accelerating the establishment of a 'climate safety net' and the formulation of a '4th Adaptation Plan' to cope with the increasing number of heatwave days, and has initiated customized adaptation measures tailored to regional climate risks [1, 8, 13, 14]. In the agricultural sector, efforts are being made to enhance climate resilience through variety development and cultivation technique improvements, with the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration inspecting climate change response status and Jangsu-gun working to discover new domestic apple varieties resilient to climate change [4, 15]. Furthermore, Busan Metropolitan City is implementing specific adaptation efforts, such as selecting climate change response projects through its 'Beautiful Landscape Award' competition and deploying 2,500 drones in heatwave-vulnerable areas to reduce heat damage to agricultural lands and workplaces [5, 17]. Goheung-gun is proactively focusing on securing agricultural water in preparation for summer droughts, and the Busan Fire and Disaster Headquarters is contributing to crisis response by providing 1,188 tons of water to drought-stricken areas [18, 19, 89].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Transition and Technological Advancement for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy and technological innovation for achieving carbon neutrality goals are actively being pursued both domestically and internationally. Australia has secured 3GW of power by converting its largest power consumers to renewable energy, and in Europe, natural gas demand is structurally decreasing due to a surge in renewable energy installations [59, 68]. Domestically, the Prime Minister discussed future energy strategies, including exploring energy mix options such as renewable energy and Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), during a meeting with Bill Gates [64, 73, 81]. Yeosu City is promoting a 50MW solar power generation project utilizing public land, and Paju City is supporting RE100 achievement by directly supplying public renewable energy to local businesses for the first time nationwide [35, 60, 74, 83]. Saemangeum is slated to develop a 'Green Energy Complex' encompassing everything from solar power generation to hydrogen production and power generation, and Samchully is expanding its carbon neutrality initiatives by utilizing biogas as a raw material for city gas [41, 72, 76]. Additionally, efforts to implement carbon neutrality are continuing in various sectors, with the green building certification system being reorganized around carbon neutrality and Ansan City introducing eco-friendly hydrogen street sweepers [27, 36, 40].

sections.title: ⚠️ Obstacles to Climate Action and Reflections for the Future
sections.content: Despite efforts to address climate change, achieving carbon neutrality goals still requires various challenges and social discussions. Concerns about achieving carbon neutrality targets were raised after Microsoft reduced its carbon credit purchases by 80% over the past year, and the government's carbon neutrality leading projects are facing difficulties due to bank collateral thresholds [25, 26]. Domestically, the National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate's amendment to the Carbon Neutrality Act drew criticism for shifting the burden of reduction onto future generations, along with accusations that greenhouse gas reduction targets were approved through a 'mechanical allocation' method without a public deliberation process [11, 28, 39]. In particular, there was strong opposition from civil society regarding the selection process for the 7 SEED technologies, where renewable energy was grouped as one, while the nuclear sector monopolized two slots [70]. Despite strong public support for expanding renewable energy, there is significant opposition to the destruction of rural residents' lives, and despite Posco International's announcement of its carbon neutrality roadmap, the fact that LNG and gas field businesses remain the backbone of its performance demonstrates the complexity of energy transition [42, 62]. These situations suggest that difficult choices are needed to save humanity from climate change, and deep reflection is required on how to communicate about these extreme climate phenomena in a reality where climate change discourse has become a battlefield of cultural wars [107, 112].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted global extreme weather phenomena, serving as a warning, and illuminated various domestic and international policy and technological efforts to overcome them. Simultaneously, we acknowledged the challenges on the path to carbon neutrality and the importance of social discourse. This concludes today's climate briefing.
